name: MAS Notice 626 — Prevention of Money Laundering and Countering the Financing of Terrorism (Banks) — revised 30 June 2025

chapters.title: Wire transfers + reliance on third parties

themes: Source of wealth + source of funds

articles.title: Scope + application
articles.requirement: Applies to all banks licensed under the Banking Act in respect of business carried on in Singapore. Group-wide application required for branches + majority-owned subsidiaries; equivalent or higher standards required for foreign branches + subsidiaries where Singapore standards are stricter than local.

articles.title: Risk-based approach + entity-wide risk assessment
articles.requirement: Bank must identify, assess + understand ML/TF/PF risks across the institution. Documented risk assessment covering customer, geographic, product/service/transaction, delivery-channel + new-technology risk factors. Refreshed at least annually + on material change (new business line, M&A, regulatory change, detected red flag). Senior-management approved.

articles.title: Proliferation Financing risk assessment (NEW 30 June 2025)
articles.requirement: Bank must integrate PF risk into the entity-wide risk assessment + customer risk profile as a distinct dimension. Aligns with FATF R.1 update (Oct 2020). Specific PF-risk indicators: DPRK + Iran nexus; dual-use goods / sensitive technology; complex ownership structures masking ultimate beneficial owners; UN-designated entities; sanctions-evasion typologies. PF controls calibrated to assessed risk.

articles.title: CDD — application triggers
articles.requirement: CDD applied: at establishment of a business relationship; on occasional transactions ≥ S$20,000 (or ≥ S$1,500 for designated cross-border wire transfers); when there is suspicion of ML/TF/PF; when there are doubts about the veracity or adequacy of previously obtained CDD information.

articles.title: CDD — identification + verification
articles.requirement: Identify the customer + verify identity using reliable + independent source documents (NRIC / passport / company registry extract / trust deed). Identify beneficial owners + take reasonable measures to verify (25% ownership threshold + senior-managing-official fallback). Understand the purpose + intended nature of the business relationship. Conduct ongoing monitoring (transaction scrutiny + record refresh).

articles.title: Enhanced Due Diligence
articles.requirement: EDD required for: foreign PEPs (always); business relationships + transactions from FATF-listed high-risk jurisdictions; complex / unusual / large transactions without apparent economic / legal purpose; correspondent banking relationships with respondent banks in jurisdictions presenting higher AML/CFT/PF risk; new products + business practices including new delivery mechanisms + new technologies. Senior-management approval; source-of-wealth + source-of-funds; enhanced ongoing monitoring; documented rationale.

articles.title: PEP obligations — foreign / domestic / IO + Singapore Government PEPs (refreshed 2025)
articles.requirement: Foreign PEPs: always heightened risk + full EDD. Domestic PEPs (incl. Singapore Government PEPs holding prominent public functions in Singapore): assessed on a risk-sensitive basis — many positions still trigger EDD based on actual risk profile (cross-border exposure, political position, sectoral risk). International organisation PEPs: similar risk-sensitive treatment. Family members + close associates within scope; 12-month tail after the PEP ceases holding the function (risk-sensitive thereafter).

articles.title: Simplified Due Diligence — narrow scope
articles.requirement: Simplified CDD permitted only where the bank's risk assessment + the supranational/national risk assessment supports lower risk + the customer category is specifically permitted (e.g. publicly-listed companies subject to disclosure rules + their wholly-owned subsidiaries; Singapore Government entities). Does not exempt from any CDD obligation; permits delayed verification within strict limits.

articles.title: Wire transfers + Travel Rule
articles.theme: Source of wealth + source of funds
articles.requirement: Banks must include complete originator + beneficiary information on cross-border wire transfers in line with FATF R.16 (Travel Rule). Cross-border wire transfers ≥ S$1,500: full information required. Domestic wire transfers: simpler requirements (account number or transaction reference). Intermediary + beneficiary banks must verify presence of required information.

articles.title: Reliance on third parties for CDD
articles.theme: Source of wealth + source of funds
articles.requirement: Bank may rely on a third party to perform CDD steps (identification + verification + beneficial ownership + purpose) only where: (a) the third party is regulated, supervised + monitored for AML/CFT/PF + has measures in place to comply with CDD + record-keeping; (b) the bank obtains the required information immediately + can obtain CDD documentation upon request without delay; (c) the bank remains responsible for CDD.

articles.title: Suspicious Transaction Reporting (streamlined 2025)
articles.requirement: Bank must promptly file STRs with STRO (via STRONet) when it knows or has reasonable grounds to suspect that any property is connected to: drug trafficking (CDSA); other serious crime (predicate offences per CDSA); terrorism financing (TSOFA); proliferation financing. The 2025 refresh streamlined: clearer trigger thresholds; structured STR content requirements; explicit PF reportability; emphasis on quality + timeliness.

articles.title: Tipping-off prohibition (CDSA s.48 + TSOFA s.12)
articles.requirement: Bank + staff prohibited from disclosing to a customer or third party that an STR has been filed or that an ML/TF investigation may be carried out. Limited carve-outs: sharing with regulators (MAS, STRO, foreign FIUs via Egmont channels); intra-group sharing for ML/TF purposes under specific safeguards; legal advice.

articles.title: Sanctions + targeted financial measures
articles.requirement: Banks must implement programs to comply with UN + Singapore targeted financial measures: real-time customer + transaction screening; freezing of designated-person funds; reporting to MAS + Attorney-General's Chambers; non-engagement with designated persons. Particular operational focus on DPRK (UNSCR 1718 + Singapore implementing notices) + Iran (UNSCR 2231 + UK + EU coordinated measures + Singapore implementation). Specific focus on shell company structures + dual-use trade.

articles.title: Internal policies + procedures + governance + AML compliance officer
articles.requirement: Documented written AML/CFT/PF internal policies, procedures + controls; senior-management approved; reviewed at least annually + on material change. Designated AML compliance officer at senior-management level (independent + sufficient seniority + resources + access to senior management); alternate compliance officer. Independent audit + compliance-function review of the AML programme. Transaction-monitoring + screening systems calibrated to the risk assessment + tuned periodically.

articles.title: AML/CFT/PF training (refreshed 2025)
articles.requirement: All employees with AML/CFT/PF-relevant responsibilities trained on: applicable laws + MAS Notice 626 + internal policies; current ML/TF/PF typologies + red flags (incl. 2025 PF-specific scenarios); their role in the AML/CFT framework; how to escalate suspicion; tipping-off prohibition. Refresher training on regulatory + typology changes. Records retained; training effectiveness assessed.

articles.title: Record retention — minimum 5 years
articles.requirement: CDD documentation + business correspondence + transaction records retained for at least 5 years after the end of the business relationship or the completion of the occasional transaction; longer where ongoing investigation or supervisory request. Records sufficient to enable reconstruction of individual transactions + accessibility to STRO + MAS on request.
